Re: Public Records Act Request

Dear Alpine Community Planning Group Members,

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I am writing to request a copy of the records detailed below.

I am researching how the Alpine Community Planning Group (ACPG) conducts its business on the part of the residents of Alpine in preparation for publication of an expose. To that end, I request the following records:

1. All Alpine Community Planning Group Agendas and Minutes from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025.

2. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another member(s) of the Alpine Community Planning Group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

3. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another government agency, including between the group members and the County of San Diego from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

4. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and any member of the public, including between the group members and individuals/entities with business before the group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

Please note that the Public Records Act allows a member of the public to request records by describing their content, rather than asking for specific documents by name; an agency that receives such a request must “search for records based on criteria set forth in the search request.”

Public records represent “any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, photocopying, transmitting by electronic mail or facsimile, and every other means of recording upon any tangible thing any form of communication or representation, including letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combinations thereof, and any record thereby created, regardless of the manner in which the record has been stored.” (Government Code section 7920.545.)

1. This request applies to all records in your agency’s possession, including documents created by a member of another government agency or a member of the public.

2. If specific portions of any documents are exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions.

3. Please provide entire documents, even if only parts of them are responsive to this request.

If you maintain records or data in electronic format, please provide them in that same format.

1 California First Amendment Coalition v. Superior Court, 67 Cal.App.4th 159, 165-66 (1998).
2 See California State University v. Superior Court, 90 Cal. App. 4th 810, 824-25 (1999).
3 Gov’t. Code § 6253(a). versions are acceptable) to avoid copying costs.
4 If you are unable to reproduce electronic records in electronic form, please provide a reason for doing so.

I request that you waive copying fees because I have limited resources, and the information requested will be used in the public interest to further the public’s understanding of the local community planning group action. None of the information obtained will be sold or distributed for profit. If you are unable to waive the copying fees, and you anticipate that these costs will exceed $50, or that the time needed to copy the records will delay their release, please contact me so that we can arrange to inspect the document or decide which documents we wish to have copied. Otherwise, please copy and send them as soon as possible. Please respond to this request within ten (10) days, either by providing all the requested records or by providing a written response setting forth the legal authority for withholding or redacting any document and stating when the documents will be made available.

If you require any clarification in identifying responsive documents or focusing this request, please contact [redacted]. Please send all records responsive to this request to Louis Russo.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[redacted]

emails.body:
Steve HalesDirector Friends of Loveland Reservoir

Hello Steve,

Steve, I want to express my sincere gratitude to you and your board for the commendable actions you've taken in support of Sunrise to Sunset. Your efforts have not gone unnoticed and are greatly appreciated. 

Have you reached out to Congressman Issa? Our easement is primarily a federal issue, and while we need follow-through, and community support everywhere we can get it, Congressman Issa is our strongest ally where the Forest Service is concerned. Please ask your board to promote a quality petition for progress on the restoration of  Sunrise to Sunset access ASAP.  As you said recently, agencies like to work with and respond to groups like Friends of Loveland Reservoir. If you need help, please let me and others know, perhaps via membership and a website.  

Your help at the ACPG is important:The ACPG has been a good base at times for Loveland Advocacy but there have been let downs too. Your board members know that  I went to a half dozen meetings with the Alpine Community Planning group for help with Loveland in the year before it was drained and to many meetings since. In the spring of 2022 a strong vote passed by ACPG to encourage Sweetwater to come to the Alpine Group. There was a least one previous resolution to write letters of support on recreation themes.  However, the chair did not complete these tasks despite the strong votes. The same thing appears to be happening with April's nearly unanimous vote for a letter of support from the ACPG on the Sunrise to Sunset. I believe you are aware through CC'd email on this trajectory. We need to work together so the ACPG honors community work and interests at Loveland and the work of the people on the planning advisory board itself on behalf of Loveland Reservoir so we can have success on Sunrise to Sunset and full defense of future complete dewatering which are here. We all agree that land use organizations are falling short of legal easement adherence and should be advised and strenuously petitioned to do otherwise. 

Please check your emails from me about Sweetwater's goal to float 200 acres of solar panels at Sweetwater Reservoir. 

The minimum water levels to float that industrial-type project will likely come from Loveland Reservoir and create new cyclical dewatering episodes. Sweetwater refuses to remove the threat, which is a factor. The good news is that it is being challenged locally in South Bay and here by us. 

Appreciatively,

Russell

emails.subject: Report on SANDAG's October Meetings to the Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
emails.body:
Good Evening APG Members,

Please note our next APG meeting will be in-person on Saturday, January
4th, 2025, from 10:00am to noon at the Lakeside Library.

*APG Announcement to SANDAG Board on Oct. 25th:*
We have good news. The second wildfire and emergency evacuation tour was
held last Friday for SR-94. Organizing the tour were SANDAG's Ariana Galvan
and Jamul-Dulzura Community Planning Group member, Paul Dombkowski. In
addition to several members from the Planning Group and SANDAG there were
participants from Caltrans, San Diego County Sheriff's office, and CalFire,
including Battalion Chief, Sam Friedman. The unincorporated communities
value the partnership and collaboration these tours create as we work
toward a safer travel experience for all. Thank you.

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report on Oct. 11th:*
-Mario Orso said that they were cooperating with the Independent Auditor
and working to build openness and trust.
-Regarding taking the 125 out of the Regional Plan as a toll road - would
we be in compliance with CARB (California Air Resources Board). We would
barely be meeting our GHG emissions and VMT measure.
-Otay Mesa East has 65% of the design completed.

APG comment to Board: Mario, this is October, wildfire season in the rural
areas. What have we done to alleviate the bottleneck issues with the
highways that are used for evacuation heading west? There are bottlenecks
that have been there forever and we've highlighted those as being potential
fatal zones for evacuees. Where are we with resolving bottleneck issues
with lanes that are one lane, two, three, that are continuing to change as
people evacuate west? Thank you. (32:00/ Oct. 11)

SANDAG reponse (Mario Orso): What route did you mention?

APG response: This would be specifically 67, but there are bottlenecks on
other evacuation routes.

SANDAG response (Mario Orso): Everett, do you want to help me on what's the
emergency evacuation plan from Caltrans?

Caltrans response (Everett Townsend): Yeah, so Caltrans has been working
with emergency responders, CalFire, CHP and others to reassess on an annual
basis, is what we do to reassess our highway system. And, to identify where
additional improvements may be made. Over the last few years, Caltrans has
completed projects there that create some widening and create opportunities
to improve traffic flow through there. Most of those issues that state
route 67 project is at some point will be presented here at the Board, but
you know, just to be informed that Caltrans is well aware of the concerns
of the communities in Ramona and further east. As well as CHP and CalFire.
And, we certainly have a plan to address any issues that may come up during
this time.

*State Route 125 Toll Removal Oct. 11th and 25th:*
Oct. 11th, Mario Orso, reported that a pre-environmental analysis and an
equity analysis need to be performed and these two actions will take one
year.

Vivian Moreno, City of San Diego comment: I continue to be extremely
disappointed with how SANDAG is handling the 125. We're the only community
(South Bay Area) that gets tripled taxed on this toll. We pay taxes every
single year. We pay the toll and we pay Transnet funding. We're the only
community that does this. This seems to me like we are slow walking this
issue.... How much longer do we have to wait? 2042?

Oct. 25th Courtney Ruby, SANDAG Independent Performance Auditor, reported
that the Executive Management Team which included former CEO, Hasan
Ikhrata; were aware of and actively working to resolve major issues with
the 125 Tolling System, yet failed to notify the Board of this until
October of 2023. Fully 18 months passed before the Board was informed of
these significant issues impacting residents of the South Bay Region. A
single-source contract was presented and approved by the Board in January
of 2024 based on the Boards belief that they could rely on the
recommendations of Executive Management. As it turned out this contract
between SANDAG and Deloitte to manage the 125 Toll Road systems was
deficient and absent an exchange of basic system requirements.

Ed Musgrove, City of San Marcos comment: We were lied to by the Executive
Team. Until the names of those in charge are revealed I have no confidence.

*Wildfire Evacuation Tour SR-94:*
On Friday, October 18th members of SANDAG, Caltrans and the Janual
Community Planning Group completed an evacuation tour. Please see Paul
Dombkowski's report sent in a previous email on October 23rd.

*News:*
At the October 11th and 25th SANDAG Board meetings we had zero voting
representation from anyone living in the Unincorporated Area. Only Nora
Vargas was present to vote on behalf of the County. Chair Vargas lives in
Chula Vista according to her profile.

*Questions from APG members*
*No questions received this month.*

Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from
SANDAG's Board of Directors website:
https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Report Submitted by:
Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

Good Afternoon APG Members,

*SANDAG CEO, Mario Orso Report:*
-Mario Orso reported that the California Air Resources Board (CARB)
accepted SANDAG's methodology for measuring GHG and, therefore, SANDAG can
continue with planning.
-A joint committee meeting between Borders, Regional Plan and
Transportations committees to present the Regional Plan. On track to meet
GHG and air quality conformity targets. This keeps funds flowing to SANDAG,
the region and the city.
-Congratulated North County Transit District for 30 years of service.

*Economic and Budget Outlook:*
Job growth is slowing. Sales tax revenue is down. Source of project funds:
State 37%, Federal 36%, TransNet 16%, Other Local Funds 11%.

Terry Gaasterland, City of Del Mar comment: ...."We are in turbulent
times....And, I would really encourage us to be incredibly careful and
conservative as we go forward into the next six months of our budgeting..."

APG Comment to Board: My question is on the job gains and losses forecast.
I have two questions. What consideration was given to the impacts of AI on
the professional, technology, transportation and housing sectors? And, my
second question is do you anticipate a reduction in healthcare sector jobs
as restrictions on our immigration policy take effect? And, the reason I
ask that is that over the last few years the State of California had opened
up Medi-Cal coverage for all who are financially eligible, regardless of
immigration status. In the County of San Diego one-third of the population
receives this coverage. So, that would be a substantial change in
healthcare.

Naomi Young, SANDAG: I think you mentioned all important factors that can
be a source of a drag on our economy and our job creation. We didn't do a
forecast on jobs, we just presented how 2024's data on unemployment has
ended. Well what we saw between 2023 and 2024, looking at where we've seen
the sector impacts and the job growth in 2024 is what makes us think that
2025 will be more of a slow job creation environment rather than a
rebound...the message is volatility, differences in local conditions from
the national and that there are some very strong potential headwinds that
give us cause for caution.

*SR-125 Toll Operations Update:*
SANDAG is actively supporting legislation to assist the implementation of
SANDAG Board Resolution 2023-11, "Declaring support of eliminating the debt
and toll-only operations on the SR-125 by 2027."

*TransNet Regional Transportation Congestion Improvement Program Proposed
(RTCIP) Fee Adjustment:*
SANDAG approved this yearly fee adjustment to be 6% effective FY beginning
July 1, 2025. This 6% increase in RTCIP fees is to keep pace with the cost
of building the roadway infrastructure needed as housing increases. The fee
is collected by each of the 18 cities and the County as part of building
fees paid by the private sector for each new housing unit. Fee will
increase from $2875.06 to $3047.57, per unit.

without a County Supervisor present.

action such as a censure because I have seen that done recently at a city
when the Board member is not fulfilling their obligations. Is that
something that could be considered on behalf of the over 500,000 people who
were not represented here by a vote today? Thank you.

Alfred Smith, SANDAG Council: I can look into that. I know we have an

emails.subject: Sequan Truck Trail Potential Battery Storage Project
emails.body:
Dear Mr. Lyon,

We were at last weeks (9/26/24) Alpine Planning Group meeting.  We would like you to add our emails to your list for any updates on progression of this very impractical venture.  Living in one of the highest fire zones and living on a street where we only have one way in and one way out, it seems so dangerous and illogical to approve a project like this.  It seemed apparent that after additional information at the meeting, it would not be an “if” there was a fire but “when” there would be a fire.  Additionally, if there was one, the water with the chemicals released would have unknown effects on our ground water, being that we are all on wells.  It’s extremely challenging to get fire insurance, and we can’t fathom how that will be affected.  Our assets are completely tied up in the value of our land and home, and fear this would be greatly compromised.
We know you heard the group loud and clear and hope your responses will reflect our great concern for this permit to be approved.

Thank you for your support on our behalf.

Sincerely,

Craig and Karen Knox
